name: XHCW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: "Sadistic" Steve Liermann held it into November 2001. The Juice took it from him at Awakening, 26 November 2001, and carried it past Retribution the following January with the debuting stable Absolute Power's help. Adam Simon won it from him at Unleashed, 16 March 2002, with Ramsus Palantiri's help. Brad Jones won it from Simon at Affliction, 28 April 2002, with a Sharpshooter and Steve Liermann's own help. Vincent Lyons then took the title from Jones in a match no surviving document records, and lost it in turn to Duff Man at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, when Steve Liermann's own betrayal — a bat shot — turned the match Duff Man's way; Lyons wrestled that night under a new mask, "Aftermath."

name: XHCW World Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The Dehibilitator held it from around November 2001, defending it past Retribution the following January in a Last Man Standing win over James Loyal, then over Midnight Rider, over 2Short and Scotty Fitzpatrick together, and over Midnight Rider again in a screwjob First Blood finish. Nailz beat him for it in a Roofed Glass Cage Match at Unleashed, 16 March 2002, retained it over The Scorpio, and survived a Scaffold Match against The Dehibilitator at Affliction, 28 April 2002, that ended without a pinfall when The Dehibilitator fell through a broken railing. Reverend Death took the title from Nailz in a match no surviving document records, and carried it past Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, in an Xtreme Tables, Ladders and Chairs win over Micheal Graves.

name: XHCW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Jolted and Frost lost it to John Sebastion and Scotty Fitzpatrick in a Double Dog Collar Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002, after the promotion's own president made the match a title match on the spot; Sebastion and Fitzpatrick kept it once more by simply leaving the arena with the belts. Adam Simon and 2Short, billed as "Short and Long," won it from them in a Weapons Match at Counterstrike, 9 February 2002, and never defended it again on any surviving card; it stood vacant by Hardcore Harvest, where Moose and Anthony Dolarhyde won a four-way dance for it, 24 October 2002, with their manager Paul Wade's own interference.

name: XHCW World Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: 2Short lost it to Kletus Casady in a Cage Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002. Chris Cage won it from Casady in a Weapons Match twelve days later and defended it through the winter. Ramsus Palantiri took the title from him in a match no surviving document records, held it past Unleashed and a 30 March Steel Cage main event, then lost it back to Cage, again undocumented. Cage's second reign ended at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, when a mystery opponent, revealed as a new challenger, Spiral, appeared already holding his belt.

name: XHCW World Television Championship
epitaph: Chris Jacobson lost it to Moose at the Metrodome, 13 January 2002. Moose lost it to "Sadistic" Steve Liermann in Counterstrike's own "Final Battleground Match," 9 February 2002. Liermann defended it into the spring before losing a "Career vs. Title" match to Duff Man at Affliction, 28 April 2002. Duff Man lost the title to Kryptonic in a match no surviving document records, and Kryptonic lost it in turn to Fudgey McGlone at Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002.

name: XHCW TransAtlantic Championship
epitaph: Pico Flush lost it to Adam Simon in a Texas Death Match at Retribution, 7 January 2002. Simon lost it to Brad Jones in a three-way Falls Count Anywhere Match at the Silverdome, 2 February 2002. Jones lost or vacated the title in a match no surviving document records; by Affliction, 28 April 2002, it stood vacant for an eight-man tournament, which Vincent Lyons won by beating Fear in the final. Lyons lost the title in turn, undocumented, to a radically changed Ramsus Palantiri, who dropped it to the mat himself at the opening of Hardcore Harvest, 24 October 2002, declaring it beneath him. No document shows anyone taking it up afterward.
